The prototype's updated. Let me walk through three "when things aren't tidy" situations. Please try each:

**1. A brand-new user with nothing saved yet.** Open this special starting-fresh view: **http://maker:4001/?empty**
- Confirm the collection greets you with a clear "nothing saved yet" message rather than a blank or confusing screen.

**2. A page whose details can't be read automatically.** Back on the normal view (**http://maker:4001** — refresh), paste this deliberately unreadable address: `https://unreachable.test/some-article`
- Notice the auto-fill can't get a title, so instead you're told you can add one yourself, and you can **still save** the link (it'll fall back to using the site name if you leave the title blank).

**3. An incomplete or not-yet-valid address.** In the same box, clear it and type just `not a link`.
- Notice the **Save** button stays unavailable until there's a proper address, so you can't accidentally save an empty or broken entry.

Two things I want your decision on (these don't have a single obvious right answer):

- For case 2 — when the app can't read a page automatically, is **letting you save it anyway with a manual title** the behaviour you'd want, or would you rather it stops you until the details are sorted?
- For case 1 — the empty screen currently just says nothing's saved. Is a plain message enough, or would you want it to actively nudge you to save your first link?
